findings.evidence: `rg -n "theorem relativeDiffCongr.*_apply"` gives lines 185, 192, 217, 225 with no attributes; Mathlib’s analogous `fixingSubgroupEquivFixingSubgroup_coe_apply` is tagged `@[to_additive (attr := simp)]`.
findings.fix: Mark these four normal-form lemmas with `@[simp]`, matching the analogous `fixingSubgroupEquivFixingSubgroup_coe_apply` API, unless there is a demonstrated loop.
findings.issue: The coercion-characterization lemmas `relativeDiffCongrOfImageEq_apply`, `relativeDiffCongr_apply`, `relativeDiffCongrOfImageEq_symm_apply`, and `relativeDiffCongr_symm_apply` are unannotated, so `simp` will not rewrite the underlying diffeomorphism of the relative equivalence to `diffCongr`/`diffCongr e.symm`.

summary: The relative conjugation surface is mostly scoped to the target, but its main coercion-characterization lemmas are missing the expected normal-form automation. Consumers can compute pointwise with `simp`, but cannot normalize the underlying diffeomorphism of the subgroup equivalence without naming the lemmas manually.
